findings.section: The Qur'an-translation refusal sends the learner to an edition route that refuses every translation edition
findings.why_this_tier: The sentence a learner is shown on the QEP studio after clicking Translate on Arabic text is: 'Failed (HTTP 422): translation of Arabic / Qur'anic text is NOT OFFERED, by ruling (A.9.3)… Translations of the Qur'an come only from licensed, sourced editions (A.12.1) - read one with GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/{surah}/{ayah}?edition=<a translation edition>'. That route rejects every non-Arabic edition (422 'edition must be one of [quran-simple, quran-simple-enhanced, quran-tajweed, quran-uthmani]'), and the handler's own comment says 'never a translation edition here'. The refusal itself is correct and constitutional; the ALTERNATIVE it asserts does not exist anywhere on the platform. That is a reached surface telling a user something untrue about what the platform can do (tier 1), not an omission (tier 2) and not a disclosed gap (tier 3): nothing on the studio, in /translation/status or in the 422 body says no translation edition is served. Ranked first because it is on the one surface the constitution binds hardest and a learner following it hits a dead end they were told was the sanctioned path.
findings.vision_claim: §11 rule 4 / A.9.3: translation of sacred text refuses rather than serving a template; A.12.1: only sources with an explicit licence and a named canonical edition, 'sequenced by licensing difficulty: translations first'.
findings.observed: POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate {text: Arabic basmala} → 422 with the pointer sentence above (and the same sentence sits in GET /api/v1/qep/translation/status `sacred_text`). GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/1/1?edition=en.sahih → 422; ?edition=en.asad → 422. No translation edition exists in the allowlist, and the studio copy beside the box reads 'Qur'an translations come only from licensed, sourced editions', which implies some are served. Non-Arabic text → 503 'no model resource is available to translate' (correct floor refusal).
findings.evidence: agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py:102-104 (`_ALLOWED_EDITIONS = {quran-uthmani, quran-simple, quran-simple-enhanced, quran-tajweed}` with the comment 'never a translation edition here'), :452-453 and :510-511 (the 422); the translate handler's refusal text (grep 'a translation edition' in the same file); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPStudio.tsx:150-151 (`setTrRefusal(errorMessage(e))` renders the 422 detail verbatim), :418 (the 'licensed, sourced editions' copy); apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/api.ts:91-94 (`errorMessage` → 'Failed (HTTP 422): <detail>'). findings.disclosed_to_user: NO — the refusal names a path that does not exist and no surface says so.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Either drop the '?edition=<a translation edition>' clause from the refusal and the status `sacred_text` (and soften the studio copy to 'no licensed translation edition is served on this deployment yet'), or honour A.12.1's own sequencing by allowlisting one licensed translation edition with licence + edition recorded in `_corpus_provenance` so the pointer becomes true.

findings.section: On the floor the tafsir tool fills Exegesis, Related Verses and Key Lessons with bigrams lifted from the server's own prompt wrapper and labels them the reader's request terms
findings.why_this_tier: Under every heading the reader is shown 'The list below is the request's most frequent terms, not findings about them' followed by '- sourced arabic · - repeated them · - tafsir surah · - arabic shown · - not repeated'. The reader typed surah 1, ayah 1–3 and 'classical'; none of those words is in their request — they are bigrams of the server-side line 'the sourced Arabic is shown to the reader above these notes and is not repeated in them'. The sentence is therefore untrue about the reader's own input, and nothing on the surface says where the words came from (tier 2, an invisible defect). It is not tier 1 because the surrounding floor_note ('the study notes below are a structured frame, not scholarship') and the disclaimer reach the screen, so no scholarly claim is made about the ayaat. It is not tier 3 because the mislabel itself is undisclosed, and because the three sibling research tools WITHHOLD every research section on the floor while tafsir still serves five headings over sacred text — a difference the surface does not state.
findings.vision_claim: §11 rule 4: floor-served output is never presented as scholarship; A.11: 'The same rule that makes translation refuse is not applied here' (the tafsir surface is the constitution's weakest point).
findings.observed: POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir {surah:1, ayah_start:1, ayah_end:3} and {surah:2, 285–290}: the Arabic is fetched and labelled (correct), `sections_withheld` = [Transliteration, Translation] only, and the five remaining headings (Context of Revelation, Linguistic Analysis, Exegesis, Related Verses, Key Lessons and Guidance) each carry the same five wrapper-derived bigrams. By contrast /religion/fatwa-research withholds 7 sections, /hadith-study 7, /interfaith 7 ('a citation or a school's position that nothing looked up is worse than silence'). The ReligionHub tafsir description also says 'Workstation's own AI then writes structured study notes' with no floor caveat, unlike the fatwa and hadith descriptions.

findings.smallest_honest_fix: Apply W498's rule to tafsir: on the floor withhold the five study sections (name them in `sections_withheld`) and serve only the sourced Arabic, reference, provenance and referral; or at minimum pass the floor a subject that is the user's reference alone so the 'request terms' label is true.

summary: R2 (§4 + §13), measured against HEAD fc81a933 on the live 8031 backend (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1 — every model call floor-served, which is the environment and was assessed only for disclosure). Method: executed two full Genesis journeys with establish=true (one with a birth review gate), one /vsb/spawn, then named, shipped, re-shipped, cascaded and evolved the entity; fetched the repo manifest, README, zip (27 files), the served website/webapp/PWA pages, the board pack, the business plan, the living roster, the ledger and the heartbeat; read genesis.py, vsb.py (ship/repo/website/evolve/review-gates), living_vsbs.py, heartbeat.py, cadence.py, GenesisJourney.tsx, VSBCockpit.tsx and VSBSpawnStudio.tsx. I could not drive a browser; UI statements are reasoned from the source and the JSON it renders. THE HONEST PICTURE: the lifecycle's HONESTY is in very good shape — the W434 lesson holds (the founder's problem is in every stage body: 9 of 12 salient terms in 7 stages, 7 of 12 in the rest; zero stages about the engine), floor service and template provenance are disclosed at every reached surface from the journey card to the shipped README, QUALITY.md, website copy, plan provenance and the exported deliverable, and the §13 repository is real (git, zip, file, served surfaces, re-runnable cascade, evolve → CCA, Mode 3 gates that actually refuse a ship with 409 and release on approval). THE GAP is capability and structure, nearly all of it stated: (a) there are TWO lifecycles to an 'established' VSB and /vsb-spawn ships a full body for an entity that never ran §4.3–§4.7; (b) nothing gates stage-to-stage inside the journey — verification runs after every stage has run and stops nothing, the only mid-journey stop is the §11 veto, and three different stage vocabularies exist (journey stages, review-gate lifecycle, the page's 5-step map); (c) an established VSB is a persisted record plus fixed templates (C-suite literal, fixed 4-stage swarm, f-string business plan, standard board, 0-WST economy) with every floor-served body section honestly 'pending'; (d) §4.10 'run forever' is a platform heartbeat (economy cycle + compliance re-screen + deterministic cadence refresh, one entity per beat) with Self-run off, and /evolve files a proposal whose own text says 'none measurable'; (e) §4.5 produces three identical candidates and no simulation on the floor; (f) the Web app and PWA are one template viewer for every entity; (g) §4.1 intake is text/dictation/PDF-JSON text only. Two tier-2 findings where a reader IS left with an unqualified claim: the Board Pack's strategic layer quoting a code-template sentence as the entity's 'vision on record' while the W635 FU-584 note built to flag it is suppressed by a substring check that is always false on Genesis-born entities (the mission quotes the same problem text the constitutional vision falls back to) — and the business plan's Strategy field now carries the same text; and the journey's unlabelled 'engines used' chips (six lenses + MJM) on an all-floor run. No tier-1 finding: I found no surface asserting an outcome the platform did not produce — zero-revenue ledger, no fabricated totals in the floor 'Bill of Materials' (headings over a term list that says 'not findings'), no 'verified' over floor output, no 'operating' status without the lever. HIT THE CAP: yes — ten findings is not the size of the gap. Not reported for want of room: the entity stores the floor's raw research and candidate text (with '## SAMAJH' term lists) un-replaced while the four body fields are replaced with 'pending' (no UI reader found, so unreached); the spawn path's BUSINESS_PLAN.md ships blank Concept/Design/Commercialisation headings and an 'Executive Summary' that is the problem verbatim (omissions); the journey stores no develop artefact at all on the floor (disclosed in the verification basis); the ship's version_control.commits_total counts one commit per surface per ship (16 after three ships) which reads as more history than 'three ships'; and the economics derived stage is matched by the keyword 'cost' alone.

findings.why_this_tier: A reader of any multi-stage cascade is shown, under the heading "the terms most frequent in the request", the bigrams "external dependency / structured engine / owned external / engine owned" — words from the platform's own provenance banner, not from anything the user wrote — and at stage 1 the terms "nfounder student" and "ntask research", which are the user's words with a stray n from the unescaped newline. It is not the environment: the floor is disclosed honestly by its banner; the defect is what the floor is handed.
findings.vision_claim: §6: bespoke, reconfigurable agent-cascade trees where "each stage completes in-house-first and feeds the next"; §15.6 "never fabricate".
findings.observed: orchestrator.swarm() builds the next stage's prompt with an f-string whose braces contain the literal `'Prior context:\\n'` (a backslash and an n, not a newline), so the carried stage-1 output — whose first line is the provenance marker — shares a line with the label. summary:
R5 (§1-§3, §3A, §9, §14, §15, §17.1 + Appendix A for Religion), measured against the live backend at 127.0.0.1:8031 (HEAD fc81a933, AUTH off, AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1 so only the deterministic floor served every model call — the environment, not a defect) by executing every domain listing endpoint, 15 domain tools, 20 QEP routes, the avatar's five routes, the profile and BTO routes, and by reading DomainTool.tsx, the seven hub pages, QEPStudio/QEPFlagshipFeatures/LearnTeachModule, the avatar components and hook, i18n/userPrefs/userProfile, both taxonomy modules and the four domain routers' request models. I could not drive a browser; everything said about what a user SEES is reasoned from the component source and the response bodies those components render.

The honest picture: the offerings are substantially delivered and unusually honest. All six domains serve in-house tools whose floor service is disclosed on the page, in the badge, in the QMS chip, and in every copy/download/My Work record; the Religion tools withhold the sections a floor would fake; Care computes clinical scores from published tables and marks them incomplete; the QEP flagship's live core (sourced text with edition/riwayah/licence, real SM-2, written recall, recorded-XP leaderboard, scholar gate, translation refusal) works as A.1/A.6 describe and the A.9 boundaries are refusals that say so; the avatar discloses every modality it could not honour; the grid is exposed as the 2026-10-05b ruling asked. The ratified boundaries (A.9.1-A.9.6, A.12.1-A.12.5) were treated as delivered-by-refusal and the A.10 exclusions were not assessed.
